availableCommands.name: simplify
availableCommands.description: Find low-info comments, one-off helpers, perf issues, and reuse opportunities. (global)

availableCommands.name: autopilot
availableCommands.description: Keep a PR merge-ready by triaging comments, resolving clear conflicts, and fixing CI in a loop. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: create-hook
availableCommands.description: Create Codex hooks. Use when you want to create a hook, write hooks.json, add hook scripts, or automate behavior around agent events. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: create-rule
availableCommands.description: Create Codex rules for persistent AI guidance. Use when you want to create a rule, add coding standards, set up project conventions, configure file-specific patterns, create RULE.md files, or asks about .cursor/rules/ or AGENTS.md. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: create-skill
availableCommands.description: Create Codex Agent Skills. Use when authoring a new skill or asking about SKILL.md structure. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: create-subagent
availableCommands.description: Create custom subagents for specialized AI tasks. Use when you want to create a new type of subagent, set up task-specific agents, configure code reviewers, debuggers, or domain-specific assistants with custom prompts. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: goal
availableCommands.description: Set a goal that Codex will pursue to completion. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: loop
availableCommands.description: Run a prompt or skill in this session on a recurring or variable interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: migrate-to-skills
availableCommands.description: Convert 'Applied intelligently' Codex rules (.cursor/rules/*.mdc) and slash commands (.cursor/commands/*.md) to Agent Skills format (.cursor/skills/). Use when you want to migrate rules or commands to skills, convert .mdc rules to SKILL.md format, or consolidate commands into the skills directory. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: new-repo
availableCommands.description: Create a Codex-hosted repo for the current project and push it. Use when a project has no git remote yet and the user asks to create a repo on Codex, push the project to Codex, or set up a Codex-hosted remote; installs and signs in the origin CLI when needed. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: origin
availableCommands.description: Install, sign in, update, or repair the origin CLI for repos hosted on Codex (origin.cursor.com). Use when the CLI is missing or outdated, git push/pull fails to authenticate against origin.cursor.com, or the user asks to set up, clone, or configure Codex-hosted repos. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: rename-chat
availableCommands.description: Rename the current chat to match its focus. Use only when the user invokes /rename-chat. Optional text after the command steers the title. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: sdk
availableCommands.description: Guide users building apps, scripts, CI pipelines, or automations on top of the Codex SDK - TypeScript (`@cursor/sdk`) or Python (`cursor-sdk` / `cursor_sdk`). Use when the user mentions integrating, installing, or writing code against the Codex SDK; says `Agent.create`, `Agent.prompt`, `Agent.resume`, `agent.send`, `run.stream`, `run.messages`, `CursorAgentError`, `@cursor/sdk`, `cursor-sdk`, or `cursor_sdk`; asks to run Codex agents programmatically from a script, CI/CD pipeline, GitHub Action, backend service, or other code outside the Codex IDE; wants to pick between local and cloud runtime, configure MCP servers for an SDK agent, or handle streaming, cancellation, or errors; or is wiring Codex into an automation, bot, or REST `/v1/agents` migration. Use eagerly rather than answering from memory; the SDK surface evolves and this skill is the source of truth for the external packages. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: share
availableCommands.description: Save, back up, or share the current project on Codex — creates a repo (a saved, versioned copy that isn't public) even for users who have never used git, handling all setup automatically. Use when the user asks to save, back up, publish, or share their project on Codex, or how to not lose it. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: shell
availableCommands.description: Runs the rest of a /shell request as a literal shell command. Use only when the user explicitly invokes /shell and wants the following text executed directly in the terminal. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: split-to-prs
availableCommands.description: Split current work into small reviewable PRs. Use when the user asks to split a chat, set of changes, branch, or PR. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: statusline
availableCommands.description: Configure a custom status line in the CLI. Use when the user mentions status line, statusline, statusLine, CLI status bar, prompt footer customization, or wants to add session context above the prompt. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: update-cli-config
availableCommands.description: View and modify Codex CLI configuration settings in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json. Use when the user wants to change CLI settings, configure permissions, switch approval mode, enable vim mode, toggle display options, configure sandbox, or manage any CLI preferences. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: django-admin-docs-screenshots
availableCommands.description: Create a Django Admin user guide with reproducible screenshots (static + interactive). Use when documenting Django admin panels, multi-tenant URL behavior, or when the user asks to automate admin UI screenshots with Playwright/Chromium for MkDocs/Markdown. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: automate
availableCommands.description: Use this skill to create Codex Automations. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: deploy-with-vercel
availableCommands.description: Link this repository to a Vercel project and deploy it using the Vercel MCP tools. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: onboard
availableCommands.description: Use /onboard for a focused Codex onboarding flow that learns basic preferences, picks a first goal, and routes the user to the right next action. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: review-bugbot
availableCommands.description: Review code changes with Bugbot subagent. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: review-security

availableCommands.name: review
